assessments.reasoning: The capture comes from apache/www-site commit 01b1be9fbc5cd93b6794f5653a58b9b863807f84, content/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt, with the scoped full-file digest. Bytes [34,222) identify the title, version, month, year, and purpose. The operative grants appear in the same document.

The public-data-admission-taxonomy capture resolves to License Index docs/SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7. Its cited bytes [533,639) contain the License row. The Foundation’s identified January 2004 grant meets each element of that row.

challenge.method: Under pinned SCES-1.0 §§1–4 and Protocol stage 7, I tested whether the artifact was an application notice, a downstream exception, or the governing license. I compared its heading, grants, section 4(d), and appendix with the Index’s license and exception rows.
challenge.results: The document defines its license as sections 1 through 9 and grants rights directly. Section 4(d) distinguishes informational NOTICE content from the license, and the appendix supplies a template for applying the license. Neither supplies a separate exception or establishes that a particular work carries the grant.

limitations: Active records the intended Index mapping. This finding covers the Foundation’s pinned text. A particular work’s grant, a downstream exception, and byte equivalence with another representation each require separate evidence.
reasoning: The Apache Software Foundation’s published text identifies itself as “Apache License” and “Version 2.0, January 2004.” Sections 2 and 3 contain copyright and patent grants. The identifiable edition, operative grants, and publisher source together satisfy the Index license criterion.
